reference_use.conclusion: The pinned libraries supply the tools but none of the needed lemmas. SimonGMT has Simon's approximate tangent spaces with uniqueness and plane-support lemmas (Ch. 3), the injective weighted, Bochner and measure area formulas with Jacobian positivity, and a.e. uniqueness of within-derivatives (Ch. 2, AreaDomain). Mathlib has Rademacher, integration by parts for Lipschitz functions, L¹-density of C_c functions, smooth uniform approximation, Tannery's theorem, Lusin–Souslin and the μHE scaling and translation laws. No pinned or DAG declaration proves any of: uniqueness of approximate differentials along a set, weak-* convergence of gradients, the anti-Lipschitz bound for immersions, the chart pull-back, or the Leibniz rule with a Lipschitz multiplier. The dor_lmbsf_* analogues are decomposing and state different results. Hence there are nine new children, with the prefix dtc_bc_lc_sl_ll_ (absent from dag.json and git history), plus two accepted declarations reused with identical types: cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (2af75d6) and cmcs_cd_defect_identity (e32f0ad). Four children need imports outside the base closure: ContinuousMapDense, SmoothApprox, Chapter02.WeightedArea/AreaCritical, Chapter02.AreaDomain and Tannery. Accepted candidates already add such imports. All 11 types elaborate in the contract-mode challenge header. Lean assemblies prove the parent type from weak_limit, smooth_leibniz, orient_interior, chart_pieces and lipschitz_smoothing, and prove weak_limit, piece_gradient, piece_weak_limit and smooth_leibniz from their declared dependencies, all with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.

subproblem.title: An injective C¹ immersion is anti-Lipschitz on compact sets (supplied step 4(b), "Bi-Lipschitz chart")
subproblem.statement: Let P, N ∈ ℕ, ψ : ℝ^N → ℝ^P be C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ) and C ⊆ ℝ^N compact. Suppose ψ is injective on C and Dψ(y) = fderiv ℝ ψ y is injective for every y ∈ C. Then there is c > 0 with c|a − b| ≤ |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| for all a, b ∈ C.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P N : ℕ) (ψ : Euclid N → Euclid P) (C : Set (Euclid N)), ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ → IsCompact C → InjOn ψ C → (∀ y ∈ C, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ y)) → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ a ∈ C, ∀ b ∈ C, c * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖ψ a - ψ b‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Supplied proof of dtc_bc_lc_sl_lipschitz_leibniz, step 4(b), bullet "Bi-Lipschitz chart", lower bound, which is proved there by contradiction. The parent applies it with C = closure(Y_j) ⊆ V_j. Here it is stated for an arbitrary compact set C on which ψ and all Dψ(y) are injective. Strict differentiability replaces the integral form of the mean value theorem used there.

1. Contradiction hypothesis. Suppose no such c exists. Then for each k ∈ ℕ there are a_k, b_k ∈ C with
 |ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k)| < (k + 1)⁻¹|a_k − b_k|.
 In particular a_k ≠ b_k. If C has at most one point, this is already impossible. Put e_k := (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k|, a unit vector.

2. Compactness. C × C × S is compact, where S is the unit sphere of ℝ^N. By sequential compactness (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with a_{φ(k)} → a ∈ C, b_{φ(k)} → b ∈ C and e_{φ(k)} → e, where |e| = 1. Write a'_k, b'_k, e'_k for the subsequences, and note φ(k) ≥ k.

3. Case a ≠ b. C is bounded, so |ψ(a'_k) − ψ(b'_k)| < |a'_k − b'_k|/(φ(k) + 1) ≤ diam(C)/(k + 1) → 0. ψ is continuous, so |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| = 0, i.e. ψ(a) = ψ(b). This contradicts injectivity of ψ on C.

4. Case a = b. ψ is C¹, so it is strictly differentiable at a with derivative Dψ(a) (ContDiffAt.hasStrictFDerivAt, whose order hypothesis is (1 : WithTop ℕ∞) ≠ 0). That is, for every η > 0 there is ρ > 0 such that
 |ψ(p) − ψ(q) − Dψ(a)(p − q)| ≤ η|p − q| whenever |p − a| < ρ and |q − a| < ρ.
 Since a'_k → a and b'_k → a, for all large k dividing by |a'_k − b'_k| gives
 |Dψ(a)e'_k| ≤ |ψ(a'_k) − ψ(b'_k)|/|a'_k − b'_k| + η < 1/(k + 1) + η.
 Let k → ∞; Dψ(a) is continuous and e'_k → e, so |Dψ(a)e| ≤ η. As η > 0 is arbitrary, Dψ(a)e = 0 with e ≠ 0. This contradicts injectivity of Dψ(a), since a ∈ C.

5. Conclusion. Both cases are impossible. Hence there is c > 0 with c|a − b| ≤ |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| for all a, b ∈ C. ∎
proof_key_steps: By contradiction: a_k ≠ b_k in C with |ψ(a_k) − ψ(b_k)| < |a_k − b_k|/(k + 1).
Compactness: along a subsequence a_k → a, b_k → b and (a_k − b_k)/|a_k − b_k| → e with |e| = 1.
If a ≠ b then ψ(a) = ψ(b), contradicting injectivity on C.
If a = b, strict differentiability of the C¹ map ψ at a gives Dψ(a)e = 0, contradicting injectivity of Dψ(a).

audit.reason: All hypotheses match. Compactness supplies convergent pairs and unit secants. Distinct limiting points contradict injectivity; coincident limits contradict injectivity of the strict derivative. The argument also covers empty, singleton and zero-dimensional cases.
